newsitem.title: UK: FT backs Blair, Times chooses Eurosceptics.
newsitem.headline: FT backs Blair, Times chooses Eurosceptics.

text.p: The Financial Times on Monday gave its lukewarm backing to Labour leader Tony Blair in this week's election while the London Times opted for Eurosceptics in any party who opposed more European integration.
The Financial Times, Britain's leading business daily, said splits in the ruling Conservatives "made it all but impossible for its leaders to implement rational policies towards Europe.
"By default, that opens the door to Mr Tony Blair and Labour. This does not amount to anything like an enthusiastic endorsement," it said.
The London Times, owned by media magnate Rupert Murdoch, advised voters to support candidates who are against further integration in the European Union.
"Our endorsement in this election, therefore, falls not on a party slate but upon individual candidates whose European ideals we support," he said.
Britain's two leading tabloids -- the daily Sun and the weekly News of the World which are also Murdoch-owned -- have both backed Blair.
Labour are overwhelming opinion poll favourites to win Thursday's election and end 18 years of Conservative rule.
